messages:
sam: Observed a sudden p95/p99 regression on text-gen endpoints after the 05:00 platform rollout. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~520ms, p99 from ~300ms -> ~1.2s. Error rates are low but tail latency is killing SLAs. :eyes:

derek: I see the same on grafana — spike started at 05:12 UTC. Correlates with the host kernel update + CUDA driver bump in this rollout. Storage I/O stands out on the affected hosts (nvme qdepth spikes).

sam: Quick checks: affected hosts are gpu-pool-3 nodes (ami-2026-05-10). New packages: kernel 6.1.15, nvidia-driver 535.86, nvme-fw 2.8. Ran a repro microbenchmark (single-stream generation) and latency is stable on older hosts.

chen: Pasted some quick outputs: 
```
# on affected host
$ iostat -x 1 3
Device:         r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s rrqm/s wrqm/s r_await w_await aqu-sz  %util
nvme0n1       12.00   18.00  1024.00 2048.00    0.00    0.00  6.50   14.20  8.0   95.00
```
and dmesg shows repeated nvme timeouts: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 timed out`

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-05-12T05:00UTC completed to gpu-pool-3 (ami-2026-05-10) :white_check_mark:

sam: Repro steps (shareable):
```
# on test client
ab -n 2000 -c 8 -p payload.json -T application/json https://api.redwood/v1/generate
# or
hey -n 1000 -c 16 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' https://api.redwood/v1/stream
```
Run that against a single affected host IP and compare p50/p95/p99.

chen: Did a quick isolate: drained one node from the pool and rerouted traffic -> tail latency on pool dropped back to baseline within 90s. Reintroduced node, tail spikes returned. Suggests node-local regression not just routing.

tanya-oncall: Suggest immediate mitigation: remove ami-2026-05-10 from rotation (rollback to previous AMI), and shift traffic to dedicated-capacity pool in other region. Also rate-limit bursty clients for 30m.

derek: I'm starting a partial rollback of nvidia-driver on 5 nodes to previous 531.x. If that fixes, we can coordinate full rollback. Taking node gpu-pool-3-07 out now.

chen: Meanwhile I'll run vendor NVMe diagnostic and collect SMART + firmware logs (nvme-cli). Plan to check if new driver/kernel path changed NVMe timeout behavior.

sara: I'll update the incident runbook and notify CS + customers about degraded tail latency. Drafting a small status blurb for the status page.

sam: Quick note: model-level mitigation available — enable reduced-kv-cache/quantized variant for latency-sensitive routes as fallback. We can toggle via routing policy for the affected traffic. That reduces token work and lowers p99 while infra is stabilized.

infra-bot: autoscaler: spun up 4 extra nodes in dedicated-capacity-us-west to absorb load (policy: emergency-burst).

derek: Update: rolled back nvidia-driver on node gpu-pool-3-07 -> after reinserting, p99 dropped from 1.2s -> ~320ms on that node. Rolling to gpu-pool-3-0[8-11].

chen: NVMe diag shows increased latency with SQ depth >128 under current nvme-fw + kernel combo. Workaround: cap queue_depth with kernel parameter and set `nvme_core.default_ps_max_latency_us` lower. Vendor says known interaction with kernel 6.1 branch + fw 2.8; they're investigating.

sam: Decision: rollback driver across pool and remove the AMI from rollout. Mitigations in flight: route traffic away from affected pool, enable model fallback, cap nvme qdepth, vendor diag. Looking at timeline for full rollback and postmortem.

sara: Action items: 1) @derek finish driver rollback across 12 nodes (ETA 30m). 2) @chen collect full nvme logs and open vendor SR (SR# 2026-642). 3) @tanya-oncall update status page and CS comms. 4) Postmortem owner: @sara (RCA due EOD).

derek: Rollout status: 9/12 nodes rolled back, p99 aggregate for pool trending down. No errors on rolled nodes.

sam: OK — once pool stable, we'll re-run load and smoke tests, then reopen controlled canary if vendor provides patch. No changes to customer billing.

sara: Noted. I'll start the incident doc and tag for postmortem. Good job triage team. :thumbsup:

tanya-oncall: I'll monitor for 2h and then handoff to eng-sre for long-term mitigations.

sam: Follow-ups after stabilizing: validate kernel/driver matrix in our CI, add nvme qdepth tests into perf suite, and include flash FW matrix in deployment checklist.

chen: saving logs to /srv/incident/2287654321/ and uploading to vendor ticket.

sam: closing note: root cause looks like a regressive interaction between kernel 6.1.* + nvme-fw 2.8 under heavy queue depth with the new 535.86 driver. Final RCA pending vendor confirmation, but rollback + qdepth cap mitigated. We'll keep this incident open until vendor confirms a patch. :white_check_mark:
